A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NJ BriefBank research. All 24 pages of v2 and 26 pages of v3, including their appendices, are readable and support matching the methods, experiments, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original practitioner feedback, retrieval and fine-tuning experiments, domain-adaptation results, and reranker evaluations in Sections 3–5 and the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical evaluations and additionally reports annotation agreement, anonymization audits, and temporal robustness results.

M1.justification: The retrieval and reranking procedures, synthetic-query generation and filtering, IRAC expansion, and ModernBERT domain adaptation are retained. The added anonymization changes benchmark preprocessing without revising these retrieval algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions retain NJ OPD and PD retrieval, BarExam-QA, LePaRD, and the same training-data sources. PD still contains 170 queries, 543 relevant paragraphs, and 96,032 corpus paragraphs. Anonymization and temporal subgroup analyses operate within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same eight pretrained retrievers and fine-tuned e5 model. The ModernBERT comparison and all six zero-shot rerankers, majority baseline, and fine-tuned Qwen3 reranker are also retained in the corresponding appendix tables.

E3.justification: v3 evaluates anonymized PD text and introduces a 100-pair independent annotation check, a 50-paragraph anonymization audit, and date-stratified OPD evaluations. Existing retrieval metrics, test-only benchmark usage, reranker query split, and reported fine-tuning settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands benchmark validation beyond v2’s dataset and metric correlations. Sections 3.2 and 5.1 add annotation-consistency analysis, anonymization error analysis, retrieval robustness to anonymization, and document-age checks, supported by new Tables A4 and A9.

E5.justification: v3 first reports independent-annotator agreement using Cohen’s kappa, obtaining 0.36 on 100 query–paragraph pairs. Both versions already report five fine-tuning seeds, means, 95% confidence intervals, and correlation p-values; no increase in run count is stated.

E6.justification: v3 revises the public-benchmark result set and adds annotation, anonymization, and temporal findings. Table 2 replaces non-anonymized PD scores with anonymized scores, including Qwen3-8B Recall@5 of 37.37% to 37.08% and fine-tuned e5-large of 35.40% to 36.26%. These are different-input evaluations; v2’s zero-shot scores remain in v3 Table A9. Reranker results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The query-to-paragraph task definition is unchanged. Neither version adds or revises theoretical assumptions, mathematical derivations, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 qualifies practical-impact claims: the introduction changes BriefBank from helping streamline drafting to being designed to do so, and makes improved defender practices conditional. The conclusion also hedges the constraint attributed to domain mismatch. The central task, dataset, taxonomy, and domain-knowledge contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of annotator disagreements and anonymization/temporal robustness. New Section 8 identifies single-office and jurisdictional limits, annotation biases, and privilege/confidentiality concerns. Section 5.1 also corrects the e5 comparison from 'surpasses' Qwen3-8B to 'approaches,' consistent with the tables.

D1.justification: v3 documents Gemma 4’s 31B model and anonymization prompt, summary-display and copying safeguards, and deployment using open models in a closed system. It updates the documented code location to the Princeton lab repository. The IRAC prompt is retained, but v2’s worked expansion example is removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Promptagator, Gemma 4, Cheong et al. on responsible legal-advice policies, and Paine and Travisano on AI discovery risks. These provide synthetic-retrieval precedent and confidentiality context; the broader positioning against existing legal benchmarks remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, portions of the introduction, and the collaboration discussion are rewritten. v3 adds a Broader Impact Statement and an explicit appendix heading, with terminology and wording refinements elsewhere. Most section organization and technical exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds temporal and anonymization comparison tables and an anonymization-prompt figure. It reorganizes the appendix, formats prompts in titled boxes, converts the retained IRAC prompt from Table A10 to Figure A4, and reorders Table 1 examples. The main visual design and existing plots are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency about benchmark reliability, privacy handling, and applicability through new validation checks and explicit limitations. It also corrects the unsupported e5 'surpasses' statement. Gains are limited by fair annotation agreement, over-anonymization, and reporting inconsistencies, including 0.84 versus 0.82 for the fine-tuning correlation and differing PD Recall@5 values across Tables A5 and A7.
